thread:
maria: Privacy request from an EU customer — they want proof all PII for subject_id:12345 was removed from backups/snapshots. Legal asked for evidence. Do we need KMS decrypt access, or can we provide a signed deletion manifest? Who can grant temp RBAC for verification?

jake: Prefer avoiding raw KMS decrypt if possible. Signed manifests + keystore-signed nonce should be sufficient for legal usually. :thinking_face:

kevin: KMS decrypt on snapshots is risky — we don't hand out decrypt perms to humans. We can create an ephemeral service account that has keystore.verify/sign rights and logs are auditable. Time-limited (1h) is fine.

ashley: From legal: signed manifests are acceptable if they include a verifiable signature chain, timestamp, and deletion operation IDs. We also need redacted audit slices showing deletion jobs kicked off and completed.

maria: What's the minimal RBAC surface so ops can run the verification and we still keep keys protected? Also need to know if we must request a retention exception for audit logs older than 90 days (customer's data touches logs ~120 days old).

jake: Proposal: ephemeral role called `dsar-verifier` scoped to project with just `keystore.keys.verifySignature` and `logs.read` for the specific log segments. Sample policy snippet:```yaml
role: dsar-verifier
bindings:
  - members: serviceAccount:dsar-verifier@infra
    permissions:
      - keystore.keys.get
      - keystore.keys.verifySignature
      - logging.logEntries.list
```
Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privacy-delete-verify

ops-bot: created temp service account dsar-verifier (id: svc-dsar-892) — expires in 3600s — ticket #3245

sre-oncall: Make sure to capture the exact audit log query and export. Example cmd:```bash
# export relevant logs for subject
curl -s "https://logs.internal/export?filter=delete_job AND subject:12345&from=2023-11-01&to=2023-11-30" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" > export-12345.json
# then redact unrelated PII
jq 'del(.entries[].payload.user_email)' export-12345.json > export-12345-redacted.json
```

maria: If legal accepts signed manifests, kevin — can you sign the deletion manifest (we'll include nonce + timestamp) and drop the signed file in the secure bucket? If not, we'll use the ephemeral account to verify signatures ourselves.

kevin: I can sign the manifest. Legal, please confirm the manifest format you need (hash algorithm, nonce, timestamp). Also we need a retention-exception request for logs older than 90 days so we can search older snapshots. I'll open a compliance ticket.

ashley: Confirmed: we need SHA256 of the manifest, timestamp, signed nonce, and operation IDs. The export must have redactions for unrelated customers. Retention exception OK — please add justification + TTL on the exception.

jake: Also adding small step to scrub EBS snapshot metadata before handing anything over — no raw blob copies out.

maria: I'll file the RBAC PR for dsar-verifier and link the compliance ticket and PR here. @ashley please sign off on the manifest format when I post it. Tagging #compliance in the PR. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: compliance ticket created: COM-987 (retention exception for logs until 2024-12-31)

maria: Thanks all — I'll update when PR and signed manifest are available.
